title: Add doctest to `symbols`
body:
Alternative to !3759 

A minor concern of mine is that an added example is partly a duplication of https://wiki.fysik.dtu.dk/ase/ase/symbols.html#ase.symbols.Symbols.indices.

# Checklist: `x` (done) or `~` (irrelevant)

- [x] [I am familiar with **ASE's contribution guidelines.**](https://wiki.fysik.dtu.dk/ase/development/contribute.html)
- [x] [**Doc strings** in code changed in this MR are up to date.](https://wiki.fysik.dtu.dk/ase/development/python_codingstandard.html#writing-documentation-in-the-code)
- [~] [**Unit tests** have been added for new or changed code.](https://wiki.fysik.dtu.dk/ase/development/tests.html)
- [~] [**Changes** have been added in `changelog.d` using `scriv`.](https://wiki.fysik.dtu.dk/ase/development/writing_changelog.html)
- [~] [**Issue is resolved** via "closes #XXXX" if applicable.](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/user/project/issues/managing_issues.html#closing-issues-automatically)
author: yuzie007

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
Although in principle it isn't Atoms' job to document symbols, I agree it's a good idea to add these examples here since people don't learn about symbols otherwise.

Should we have `symbols == 'C'` since one can easily do masks this way?

For getting the unique elements I'd do `atoms.symbols.species()`, but the order is not reproducible so the doctest may fail (unless it magically knows not to test order in sets).  (Note that in the current example, `.keys()` can be removed)

Thanks a lot!

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:
Thank you @askhl for the review!

I agree on adding also the `symbols == 'C'` example, done in the revised commit. Further:

1. `.keys()` is removed for simplicity
2. `.species()` is also referred to, with skipping it in `doctest`

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: In your opinion would it be crazy to deprecate `get_chemical_symbols()` and instead ask people to use the (shorter, easier) `list(atoms.symbols)` or `[*atoms.symbols]`?  Or simply to use the symbols as they are, for the simple reason that they *are a sequence* of symbols.

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body: I would be happy to deprecate `atoms.get_chemical_symbols()` and recommend `atoms.symbols` or `list(atoms.symbols)` as appropriate. This should, of course, have a reasonable warning period before it is removed as the method is used quite a lot.

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:
Thank you so much @askhl and @ajjackson for further ideas!

I also think it fully makes sense to deprecate `get_chemical_symbols()`, since we already have similar deprecate `cell`-related methods.
I will make a follow-up MR for this:)
